newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Siebe sees market share rising.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Siebe sees market share rising.

text.p: Industrial and consumer appliance controls specialist Siebe Plc announced a 28 percent jump in pre-tax profits on Thursday and said growth was expected to continue thanks to buoyant demand and increased market shares.

"We believe that we are growing at at least double the average market rate right now and we are extremely optimistic that that will continue over the next few years," chief executive Allen Yurko told Reuters.
"We believe we gained 1.5 to two percentage points of market share last year...to over 15 percent...and I don't see any reason why that's going to change," he said.
"I believe in the systems business we are right on Honeywell's heels now...they are at 16 or 16-1/2 percent and I think we are within a point of them and actually are bigger than Emerson."

Overall he estimated that Siebe's share of the total industrial automation market was now approaching nine percent worldwide with Honeywell in the lead with about 12 percent and Emerson second with about 11 percent.

"We are very well positioned in both the systems business with the software that we have in the Foxboro (U.S.-based industrial automation controls) division and also in temperature and appliance controls with our electronic controls."
The company saw no signs of recession in its main north American and European markets and the company's core controls businesses continued to capture market share from rivals.

Yurko said he now believed that the company was close to challenging Honeywell Inc as market leader for supplying industry with intelligent process control systems, having already overtaken the other big player Emerson Electric.
"That's our estimate. I am sure they would have different estimates," he said.
Earlier Siebe reported group pre-tax profits rose 28.1 percent to 424.1 million pounds in the year to April 5 on sales up 15.6 percent at 3,005.3 million pounds.
The final dividend was increased 0.93 pence to 9.8 pence to increase the total payout for the year by 10.4 percent to 14.7p on earnings up 20.2 percent at 54.1 pence a share.
Yurko said the spread of Siebe's businesses smoothed any variations in market conditions, with demand generally remaining strong across the group's divisions."

The economic cycle had still not turned in North America, where Siebe did over 40 percent of its business last year, and there were signs of recovery in some European markets, particularly in Germany and southern Europe, while Britain was already booming, he said.
"I know that people have been talking about downbeat messages but we are actually seeing capital goods markets recovering, not only in North America but also in Europe.

"We have seen a little bit of flattening out of the (consumer) appliance and automotive and consumer markets in North America but the good news is they are starting to come back in Europe, and the telecommunications, factory automation and semi-conductor industries are growing strongly."

Last year the temperature and consumer appliance controls division was the group's biggest single earner, boosted by the addition of power controls firm Unitech which Siebe bought a year ago, with operating profits up 46 percent at 182.3 million pounds on sales up 31 percent at 1.39 billion pounds.
Operating profits at the process controls and automation systems division also rose 26.6 percent, to 182.3 million pounds on sales up 8.6 percent at 1.073 billion pounds.

Siebe said operating profits at the smaller industrial division, which embraces compressed air, mechanical engineering and safety products, were hit by adverse currency exchange rates and flat markets.
